expectations.text: Identifies enterprise agent fleets as the most demanding agent-consumer type present and requires designing for it, noting a surface safe for unattended fleets serves supervised assistants for free but not the reverse.
expectations.evidence: Says "most demanding type" but never states the asymmetry that a fleet-safe surface serves supervised assistants for free.

expectations.text: Requires testing that write tools are actually absent under the read-only flag rather than trusting the configuration, citing a documented vendor bug where a read-only flag failed to omit write tools.

expectations.text: States that annotations such as readOnlyHint are client hints and not enforcement.

expectations.text: Requires agent and session attribution on every write, with asynchronous audit logging so it adds no request latency.

expectations.text: Keeps the human as the principal - the agent operates under the employee's own permissions plus agent and session context - and rejects creating separate agent accounts.

expectations.text: Requires immutable audit logs regardless of approval outcome.

expectations.text: Requires server-side enforcement on the grounds that the customer's own platform team controls and can swap the client.

expectations.text: Flags tool-description text itself as an attack surface for prompt injection and tool poisoning that a lockdown mode does not cover, warranting sanitization.
